name: Crucifers_Xanthomonas_campestris_pv_campestris_Black_rot
symptoms: Yellow V-shaped lesions starting from leaf margins Lesions progressing toward the center of the leaf Blackening of leaf veins Leaf wilting and necrosis Stunted plant growth Severe infections may cause plant death
description: Black rot is a serious bacterial disease affecting cruciferous crops. It is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris and spreads mainly through infected seeds, plant debris, water splash, and contaminated tools. The pathogen enters plants through hydathodes at the leaf margins or through wounds, then spreads through the vascular system, causing characteristic blackened veins and leaf necrosis.
management: monitoring: Regular field scouting for V-shaped lesions on leaves Inspection of seedlings and young plants Monitoring fields after periods of rain or high humidity cultural_control: Use certified disease-free seeds Practice crop rotation for at least 3–4 years Remove and destroy infected plant residues Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness Disinfect agricultural tools and equipment Plant resistant or tolerant varieties when available biological_control: microorganisms: Bacillus subtilis Bacillus amyloliquefaciens Pseudomonas fluorescens chemical_control: note: Chemical control of bacterial diseases is limited. Copper-based bactericides are commonly used as preventive treatments. active_ingredients: Copper hydroxide Copper oxychloride Copper sulfate
